Widely applicable information criterion for mvgam models

Source: R/waic.mvgam.R
waic.mvgam.Rd

Passes the pointwise log likelihood of log_lik.mvgam() to loo::waic(). loo.mvgam() estimates the same ELPD by PSIS and reports Pareto k diagnostics that say when to distrust it. Vehtari et al. (2017) recommend it over WAIC.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam
waic(
  x,
  ...,
  compare = TRUE,
  resp = NULL,
  pointwise = FALSE,
  model_names = NULL,
  incl_autocor = TRUE,
  incl_dynamics = NULL,
  by_series = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A fitted mvgam or jsdgam object.

...

Further arguments to log_lik.mvgam(), such as ndraws.

compare, resp, pointwise, model_names

The arguments of brms::waic.brmsfit. resp scopes a multivariate fit to one response. Supplying one of the others raises an error. loo_compare() ranks several waic() results.

incl_autocor

Logical, default TRUE. Passed to log_lik.mvgam(). TRUE scores each observation under the latent trend state the model inferred at that time. The ELPD then describes the series that was observed. FALSE scores the deterministic submodel alone.

incl_dynamics

Deprecated alias for incl_autocor.

by_series

Logical, default FALSE. TRUE returns a data frame with one row per series and columns series, elpd, se_elpd, p and n_obs, as spOccupancy::waicOcc(by.sp = TRUE) ranks species. An occupancy or N-mixture fit is scored per site, each site counted in its species.

Value

A waic object (see loo::waic()), or with by_series = TRUE a data frame of per-series estimates.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing, 27:1413-1432. doi:10.1007/s11222-016-9696-4

See also

loo.mvgam() estimates the same ELPD by PSIS. lfo_cv.mvgam() scores forecasts from rolling origins. The forecast evaluation article compares models by approximate and exact cross-validation.

Other model comparison: bridge_sampler.mvgam(), compare_elpds(), kfold.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), log_lik.mvgam(), loo.mvgam(), loo_compare.mvgam_lfo(), mvgam_loo_extras, posterior_average.mvgam()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(13)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())

mod <- mvgam(y ~ s(x),
              trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
              data    = simdat$data_train,
              family  = poisson(),
              chains  = 2, silent = 2)
#> Warning: 9 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The WAIC estimate of the ELPD, with its effective number of
# parameters p_waic
waic(mod)
#> Warning: 
#> 26 (28.9%) p_waic estimates greater than 0.4. We recommend trying loo instead.
#> 
#> Computed from 2000 posterior draws and 90 log-likelihood terms.
#> 
#>           Estimate   SE
#> elpd_waic   -218.4  6.8
#> p_waic        32.8  2.9
#> waic         436.9 13.6
#> 
#> 26 (28.9%) p_waic estimates greater than 0.4. We recommend trying loo instead. 

# The PSIS estimate of the same ELPD. Its Pareto k diagnostics mark
# the observations it estimates poorly
loo(mod)
#> Warning: Some Pareto k diagnostic values are too high. See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.
#> 
#> Computed from 2000 posterior draws and 90 log-likelihood terms.
#> 
#>          Estimate   SE
#> elpd_loo   -227.1  7.8
#> p_loo        41.4  4.0
#> looic       454.1 15.7
#> ------
#> MCSE of elpd_loo is NA.
#> MCSE and ESS estimates assume MCMC draws (r_eff in [0.5, 1.4]).
#> 
#> Pareto k diagnostic values:
#>                          Count Pct.    Min. ESS
#> (-Inf, 0.7]   (good)     63    70.0%   196     
#>    (0.7, 1]   (bad)      23    25.6%   <NA>    
#>    (1, Inf)   (very bad)  4     4.4%   <NA>    
#> See help('pareto-k-diagnostic') for details.

# Next, loo_compare() ranks several models by either estimate
# }
